quick.summary: Why a number that later falls back costs trust, and how to say confidence plainly.
quick.takeaway: Give the number, the range and how sure you are.

beats.line: I said conversion rose. Next week it fell back. Do people still trust me?
Trust drops when a number sounds more certain than it was.
So I should have said nothing?
No. Say three things together. The number, a range, how sure.
Small weeks jump around, so say that too.
Won’t a range sound like I don’t know?
It sounds like you know exactly how much you know.
Conversion looks up, maybe one to three points. One week only, so early.
If it falls back now, nobody is surprised.

quiz.question: A result looks good but comes from one small week of data. How should you report it?
options: Give the number, a range, and say it is early
Report the number as a clear win
Round it up to sound stronger
quiz.explanation: Saying how sure you are lets people act sensibly and keeps their trust if it changes.

quiz.question: Giving a range instead of one number makes an analyst look less trustworthy.
quiz.explanation: A range shows you know how much the data can support, which builds trust when numbers move.
